name: Political moderate
summary: A political moderate rejects radical or extreme views and seeks a position between the main poles, usually through compromise, gradual reform and attention to the merits of each issue. Moderation is a stance about method and range more than a fixed program, so moderates hold mixed positions that vary by country, and in practice they support democratic institutions, a mixed economy with a welfare state, and coalition-building across left and right.
scope: Political moderation as the defining sources treat it: a stance that rejects radical or extreme views and seeks a position between the poles, studied as a moral virtue, an institutional effect, a sociological pattern and an ideology of the middle or third way (de Haan and Lok, s4), and as the self-described moderate position (Kabaservice, s5). It is positional and methodological, so it excludes any particular party, the programmatic strands (centrism, radical centrism, liberal centrism) and the Indian Congress 'Moderates' of 1885-1905.

furtherReading.title: Introduction: The Politics of Moderation (de Haan and Lok)
furtherReading.note: Scholarly abstract separating moderation as virtue, institutional effect, sociological pattern and ideology.

furtherReading.title: The Radicalism of Moderation (Craiutu, Niskanen Center)
furtherReading.note: A political theorist on moderation as realism, piecemeal reform and pluralism.

sources.title: Introduction: The Politics of Moderation
sources.author: Ido de Haan and Matthijs Lok
sources.usedFor: Moderation as an ideology of the middle or third way, and its relation to compromise in deep conflicts.

missingStatements.rationale: Compromise and accommodation of both sides are the defining method of moderates and centrist parties.

notes: Moderation is a positional and methodological label, so most substantive policy answers are low-confidence and many are neutral: self-described moderates divide on healthcare, guns, drugs, immigration and abortion. Medium answers mostly follow from rejecting radical or extreme proposals and from documented centrist support for gradualism, a mixed economy and democratic coalition politics. Web phase: re-read the Craiutu commentary (s6) and the Conversation piece on moderate tests; they speak to method (piecemeal reform, pluralism, compromise, nonviolence, checks and balances), so every other open statement stays null. Themes searched: government, means, liberty, society; economy and world have no moderate-specific position beyond rejecting single blueprints.
